\## Overview

This document describes Script 2 of the ATAC-seq and RNA-seq integration

pipeline. Script 2 integrates the annotated ATAC-seq differential peak

data with RNA-seq differential expression data by matching Ensembl gene

IDs between both datasets. For each of the six pairwise comparisons it

identifies genes that are both differentially accessible in chromatin and

differentially expressed, assigns concordance categories, calculates

integration scores, and saves results for downstream visualisation in

Scripts 3 and 4.

\### Integration strategy

Ensembl gene IDs are used as the primary matching key rather than gene

symbols because they are stable identifiers that do not change between

annotation versions. Gene symbols can be renamed between Ensembl releases

--- for example a gene annotated as CTRB2 in Ensembl v106 may appear as

CTRB1 in a newer version or in NCBI. Both gene symbols are retained in

the output (\`gene_name_atac\` from ATAC annotation and \`gene_name_rna\`

from RNA-seq) for biological interpretation and transparency.

\### Thresholds applied

\- ATAC-seq: padj \<= 0.05, no fold change filter. Chromatin accessibility

changes are often modest in absolute fold change terms but biologically

meaningful, so no fold change threshold is applied.

\- RNA-seq: pre-filtered by Novomagic at \|log2FC\| \>= 0.322 (FC \>= 1.25)

AND padj \<= 0.05. Files are used as delivered with no additional

filtering.

\### Concordance categories

Four categories are assigned based on the direction of chromatin

accessibility and gene expression changes:

\| Category \| ATAC log2FC \| RNA log2FC \| Biological interpretation \|

\|\-\--\|\-\--\|\-\--\|\-\--\|

\| Concordant up \| Positive \| Positive \| Chromatin more open and gene more expressed --- gene being activated \|

\| Concordant down \| Negative \| Negative \| Chromatin more closed and gene less expressed --- gene being repressed \|

\| Discordant (open/down) \| Positive \| Negative \| More open but less expressed --- complex regulation \|

\| Discordant (closed/up) \| Negative \| Positive \| More closed but more expressed --- indirect regulation \|

\## Outputs

All outputs saved in:

\`results/Script2_integration/ATAC_padj0.05_RNA_FC1.25_padj0.05/\`

\| File \| Description \|

\|\-\--\|\-\--\|

\| per_comparison/integration\_\[name\].tsv \| Full integration table per comparison \|

\| per_comparison/integration\_\[name\].xlsx \| Same as TSV in Excel format \|

\| per_comparison/venn_genes\_\[name\].xlsx \| Gene lists by category (7 sheets) \|

\| summary/integration_summary.tsv \| Summary across all comparisons \|

\| summary/integration_summary.xlsx \| Summary in Excel format \|

\### Integration score columns

\| Column \| Description \|

\|\-\--\|\-\--\|

\| concordance \| Concordance category \|

\| combined_score \| atac_log2FC × rna_log2FC --- positive = concordant \|

\| combined_pvalue \| atac_padj × rna_padj --- product of adjusted p-values \|

\| neg_log10_pval \| -log10(combined_pvalue) --- Y axis for volcano plots \|

\| weighted_score \| combined_score × neg_log10_pval --- primary ranking metric \|

\| z_combined_score \| Z-score normalised combined score --- equal weight to both datasets \|

\| sig_score \| -log10(atac_padj) + -log10(rna_padj) --- additive significance \|

\| distance_weight \| Exponential decay proximity weight (\~0.95 at 500bp, \~0.007 at 50kb) \|

\| distance_weighted_score \| combined_score × distance_weight \|

\### Note on multiple peaks per gene

The number of integrated rows exceeds the number of overlapping genes

because one gene can have multiple significant ATAC-seq peaks. Each

ATAC peak is retained as a separate row in the integration table,

preserving all peak-gene associations. This is scientifically correct

since multiple peaks near one gene all contribute to the chromatin

accessibility landscape of that gene.
